summary: Closed O-017, the second round of R2-M1. In the SL-065 rule at .taad/fitness.yaml:810, the comment span and the ScrollViewer property-element span are now tempered tokens: `<!--(?:(?!-->).)*-->` and `(?:(?!</ScrollViewer\.\1>).)*`. Each skipped span now ends at its own first closing tag instead of running on to a later `-->` in the file. I added quiet plant row S13 to eng/rules-harness/plants.json: `<!-- the texts -->` inserted after the unique `</ScrollViewer.Style>`. The `_note` is updated to 35 rows. I measured S09-S13 with harness.py's own Planting, attribute, judge and xUnit run on the harness's kept scratch copy, bypassing only its refusal of the pre-existing UNRAN import rule. All five rows came back AS-RECORDED. The previous pattern on the same S13 plant, and on a comment inside DriveScroller, produced a STRAY-HIT at 289 and 114, which makes the harness fail. Nothing under src/ or tests/ changed.

files.why: O-017: at line 810, replaced the unbounded lazy comment and property-element spans with the reviewer's tempered-token pattern, verbatim. Added one sentence to the rule's 'because': a skipped comment or property element ends at its own first closing tag, and S13 guards that.

O-017: added quiet row S13 (insert-after '</ScrollViewer.Style>', text '<!-- the texts -->', xunit quiet, fitness quiet). Its note says a regression shows up as a STRAY-HIT on the ScrollViewer's line. Updated the _note from 34 to 35 rows and described S09-S12 as fire rows and S13 as a quiet row.

obligations.how: Line 810 now carries the reviewer's tempered-token pattern, character for character, and plants.json has quiet row S13 at the unique anchor </ScrollViewer.Style>; the _note count is updated. I used harness.py's own code (load_rows, batches, Planting.apply and restore, run_xunit, run_fitness, attribute, judge) on its kept scratch tree, skipping only check_clean's refusal of the known-unran import rule. Clean: xUnit 11 Facts with no hits, fitness 62 rules with no hits. S09-S13 in one batch, as the harness batches them: S09, S10, S11 and S12 fire at offset 0, S13 is quiet in both engines, all AS-RECORDED, no strays. Each row alone gives the same results. Extra shapes with the new pattern: a comment inside DriveScroller is quiet; '>' in an attribute fires; comment + ScrollViewer.Resources + comment + DataGrid fires; a self-closing sibling is quiet; a commented TextBlock-only ScrollViewer is quiet. With the previous pattern swapped back in, S13 gives 'STRAY-HIT ... MainWindow.xaml:289' and the DriveScroller comment gives 'STRAY-HIT ... :114'. Those are the false positives the review named, and the harness exits 1 on a stray, so S13 catches the regression.

tests.note: AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 47 settled entries not compared.

Exit 2, CANNOT MEASURE, before any row ran. It is the same pre-existing cause as attempts 1 and 2: the must_not_import rule 'the provider does not use the code it checks' is UNRAN, so check_clean refuses the baseline. The file parsed and --only accepted S13. The kept scratch copy was reused for the next run and then deleted.

tests.note: Batch S09-S13: S09-S12 fitness fire/fire at spans 107-109, 110-113, 114-117 and 118-125; S13 quiet/quiet at 319; xUnit ran 11 Facts, quiet on all rows; every row AS-RECORDED, no strays. Each row alone: AS-RECORDED. Extra shapes, current pattern: DriveScroller comment quiet, gt-in-attr fire, comment+Resources+comment+DataGrid fire, self-closing sibling quiet, texts-only with comment quiet. Previous pattern: S13 gives STRAY-HIT at :289, DriveScroller comment gives STRAY-HIT at :114. No __pycache__ was written into the repo, and the scratch copy was deleted.
On the real worktree: 62 rules loaded, 0 violations, the SL-065 rule loaded with no hit. The verdict reads 'unable' only because of the pre-existing UNRAN import rule. The temp home was deleted.

Not re-run: this attempt changed only .taad/fitness.yaml and eng/rules-harness/plants.json, neither of which is in the exe, and nothing under src/ or tests/ changed since f513faf. Validate-2 re-ran B-007, C-001, S-002 and S-003 against the republished exe at HEAD. The real entry point for this change is the engine's fitness.check, which I ran on the real worktree above.

deviations: The S13 text is indented to the house style ('                        <!-- the texts -->') instead of the bare '<!-- the texts -->' the fix wrote. Whitespace is irrelevant to the pattern, and the harness matches anchors, not planted text.
One sentence was added to the rule's 'because' so it describes the bounded spans and names S13. The pattern itself is the reviewer's, verbatim.
not_built: S09-S13 were not run end to end through `harness.py` itself. It still exits 2 on the pre-existing UNRAN import rule. They were run through the harness's own planting, attribution, judging and xUnit code, with only the clean-baseline gate bypassed.
follow_ups: This is the second send-back on the same rule's pattern. The first missed house-style violations (comment, property element, '>' in an attribute). The fix for that over-reached into a false positive on legitimate comments. The rule now has fire rows and a quiet row on both sides of its boundary, which is what was missing, but the harness that would run them unattended still cannot measure. Until the harness can measure, nothing catches a third regression of this kind.

eng/rules-harness/harness.py cannot measure at this HEAD (exit 2): the must_not_import rule 'the provider does not use the code it checks' comes back UNRAN without a code graph. Attempt 2 found that fitness.check(tree, build=True) alone does not fix it, because the scratch copy has no .git or .code-review-graph marker. The fix is either to give the scratch copy a root marker or to teach check_clean about import rules known to be unran. S09-S13 should then be run through the harness.
A quiet row for a comment inside DriveScroller would pin the other site the review named. It was measured quiet here but not added, because the fix asked for one row.
